newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Two Israeli investment firms in merger talks.
newsitem.headline: Two Israeli investment firms in merger talks.

text.p: Ilanot Discount and Batucha Securities and Investments, two of Israel's biggest investment houses, have entered merger talks, the companies announced on Sunday.

The joint company, which would be one of the biggest investment management firms in Israel, would begin operations in 1997. It would be jointly owned by Clal Capital Markets and Discount Investment Corp.
Batucha is wholly owned by Clal Capital Markets, a subsidiary of Clal Israel, one of Israel's biggest holding companies.
Batucha is the largest private brokerage in Israel, managing portfolios, provident funds and mutual funds with assets of 1.8 billion shekels. It has five branches and 125 employees.

Ilanot, a major mutual fund manager, is a subsidiary of Discount Investment, itself a subsidiary of IDB Development, another major Israeli holding concern. Ilanot manages 30 funds with 1.7 billion shekels in assets.
Recently, Israeli brokerage firms and fund managers have suffered from a decline in activity in the Tel Aviv capital market, which has led to a number of mergers.
